title: Visit Rotorua on Budget
meta_desc: Discover how to visit Rotorua on a family budget of $250-450/day. Explore free activities, affordable accommodation.
intro: Rotorua is a top destination for families, offering a mix of geothermal wonders, Maori culture, and adventure activities. With some planning, you can have a fantastic time in Rotorua without breaking the bank. Here's a guide to help you visit Rotorua on a budget of $250-450 per day for a family of four.

sections.heading: Realistic Daily Costs
sections.body:
A daily budget of $250-450 for a family of four is realistic for Rotorua, considering accommodation, food, and activities. You can expect to pay around $150-250 per night for a mid-range accommodation that suits a family of four. Food prices are similar to other major New Zealand cities, with meals starting from $15-20 per person.

Activities are a significant part of the daily budget, with prices ranging from $20-50 per person for top attractions like Te Puia and Skyline Gondola. However, there are also many free activities to enjoy, such as the Government Gardens and Lake Rotorua foreshore walk.

sections.heading: Free Activities and Attractions
sections.body:
One of the best things about Rotorua is the number of free activities and attractions on offer. The Government Gardens and croquet lawn are a must-visit, and the Lake Rotorua foreshore walk is a great way to enjoy the scenery. Kuirau Park is another hidden gem, with its free geothermal park featuring bubbling mud and steam vents.

Rainbow Springs, just outside Rotorua, offers a free kiwi viewing at dusk if you purchase a daytime ticket. This is a great way to see New Zealand's national bird up close and learn more about conservation efforts.

sections.heading: Accommodation Options
sections.body:
Accommodation in Rotorua ranges from budget-friendly options like holiday parks and motels to mid-range hotels and apartments. For a family of four, consider staying in a self-contained apartment or holiday house, which can provide more space and flexibility.

Some popular accommodation options in Rotorua include the Rotorua Top 10 Holiday Resort, which offers a range of accommodation types from budget-friendly cabins to luxury apartments. Another option is the Novotel Rotorua Lakeside, which offers comfortable rooms and a great location.
list: Holiday parks and motels: $100-200 per night
Mid-range hotels and apartments: $150-300 per night
Self-contained apartments and holiday houses: $200-400 per night

sections.heading: Where to Save Money and Splurge
sections.body:
To save money in Rotorua, consider visiting during the off-season or taking advantage of package deals that include accommodation and activities. You can also save money by preparing your own meals instead of eating out.

On the other hand, some activities are worth splashing out on, such as the Te Puia geothermal park and the Skyline Gondola. These experiences are unique to Rotorua and provide a memorable experience for the whole family.
